name: garmin-health-mcp
description: Your Garmin sleep, HRV, Body Battery, stress, activities and training load via Garmin's official Personal API, with history, charts, dashboards and a readiness estimate.
long_description: Unofficial MCP server for Garmin's Personal API (launched 21 Oct 2026). Read-only. Keeps a local history so it can chart any daily metric, model Garmin-style acute/chronic load, fitness/fatigue/form, recovery time and a Training-Readiness-like estimate that calibrates to the scores your watch shows. Your data goes only between your computer and Garmin.

prompts.name: morning_briefing
prompts.description: How recovered am I and what should today's training look like?
prompts.text: Call morning_check. Give me a short morning briefing: the readiness estimate and the one or two factors driving it, how last night's sleep and HRV compare with my baseline, recovery hours left, and where my training load sits. End with a concrete suggestion for today's training (type, duration, intensity) that fits. If you know my Garmin readiness score, log it first.

prompts.name: weekly_review
prompts.description: Review the last few weeks of recovery and training.
prompts.text: Call weekly_report(weeks=${arguments.weeks}) and training_load(days=42). Review my last ${arguments.weeks} weeks: training volume and load trend, fitness vs fatigue, sleep/HRV/resting-HR trends, and anything that looks like accumulating fatigue or a good adaptation. Finish with two or three specific recommendations for next week.

prompts.name: build_dashboard
prompts.description: Make an interactive health and training dashboard from my Garmin data.
prompts.text: Call dashboard_data(days=${arguments.days}) and build a single-page interactive dashboard from it (an HTML artifact if you can publish one). Include: a header with today's readiness estimate, sleep, HRV, resting HR, Body Battery and recovery hours; HRV with its balanced band and resting HR over time; sleep score; training load with acute vs chronic and the 0.8-1.5 optimal ratio band; fitness/fatigue/form; weekly rollups; load focus; and recent activities. Embed the JSON as data, label the server's estimates as estimates, and make it work in light and dark mode and on a phone.
